subject: Science
title: Push and pull
objectives: Children will push and pull toys and say push or pull.
Children will notice that pushing moves things away and pulling brings them closer.
content: Pushing and pulling toys and objects, noticing that pushing moves things away and pulling brings them closer, and push and pull games.
teachingActivities: Use large light objects that children can move easily; say push or pull as the action happens; let children feel the effort; link to everyday actions such as opening a door.
learnerActivities: Push and pull toys on request and say push or pull with support.
resources: Toy carts and boxes with string
A door that opens both ways
assessment: Observe whether each child pushes and pulls a toy on request and says push or pull.
expectedOutcomes: Pushes and pulls a toy on request.
Says push or pull with support.

lessons.title: Pushing a toy
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will push a toy and see it move away.
successCriteria: Pushes a toy along the floor
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can explore materials, name animals and plants and care for living things.
lessons.starter: Push a toy cart across the floor and say "Push. The cart moves away."
teacherActivities: Show how to push a cart with both hands and say "Push, push, push."
Let each child push the cart gently across the floor.
Ask "Which way did it go?" and point away.
Push a soft ball and watch it roll.
learnerActivities: Child pushes the cart and watches it move.
Child pushes the ball and says push.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to push a cart with both hands and say "Push, push, push." Children: Children watch and say push.
Step 2. Teacher: Let each child push the cart gently across the floor. Children: Child pushes the cart and watches it move.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "Which way did it go?" and point away. Children: Child points away from themselves.
Step 4. Teacher: Push a soft ball and watch it roll. Children: Child pushes the ball and says push.

practical.title: Pushing play
steps: Clear a long space on the floor.
Push a cart or box across it.
Say push and watch it go.
practical.safety: Clear the floor and keep children well apart. Use light carts and push at a walking pace. Supervise closely.

differentiation.support: Push the cart together with a hand over the child’s hand.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to push the cart as far as they can.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Park the cart and say "Push, push, stop."
lessons.homeConnection: Let your child push a small cart or a toy car at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "push a toy and see it move away" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Push, push, push the cart. Push it far away.

lessons.title: Pulling a toy
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will pull a toy on a string and see it come closer.
successCriteria: Pulls a toy along the floor
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can explore materials, name animals and plants and care for living things.
resources: A light box with a handle
lessons.starter: Pull a toy on a string towards you and say "Pull. The toy comes to me."
teacherActivities: Show how to hold the string and pull the toy.
Let each child pull a toy along the floor.
Ask "Which way did it come?" and point to yourself.
Pull a light box with a handle.
learnerActivities: Child pulls the box and says pull.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to hold the string and pull the toy. Children: Children watch and say pull.
Step 2. Teacher: Let each child pull a toy along the floor. Children: Child pulls the toy.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "Which way did it come?" and point to yourself. Children: Child points towards themselves.
Step 4. Teacher: Pull a light box with a handle. Children: Child pulls the box and says pull.

practical.title: Pulling play
steps: Give each child a toy on a string.
Pull it along a clear path.
Say pull and see it come closer.
practical.safety: Use short strings and watch for tripping. Remove strings from around necks and keep strings out of reach after play.

differentiation.support: Pull the string together and say the word.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to pull a heavier box with a friend.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the toys away and say "Pull, pull, stop."
lessons.homeConnection: Let your child pull a toy on a string at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "pull a toy on a string and see it come closer" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Push or pull?
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will decide if an action is a push or a pull.
successCriteria: Says push or pull for an action
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can explore materials, name animals and plants and care for living things.
resources: Pictures of pushing a door, pulling a wagon, pushing a swing and pulling a drawer
lessons.starter: Show a door and say "To open this door we push." Pull a drawer and say "To open this drawer we pull."
teacherActivities: Show each picture and do the action.
Ask "Is it a push or a pull?"
Let children try pushing and pulling real objects.
Match each picture to push or pull.
learnerActivities: Children look and copy the action.
Child pushes a door or pulls a drawer.
Child places the picture in the right group.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show each picture and do the action. Children: Children look and copy the action.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "Is it a push or a pull?" Children: Child says push or pull.
Step 3. Teacher: Let children try pushing and pulling real objects. Children: Child pushes a door or pulls a drawer.
Step 4. Teacher: Match each picture to push or pull. Children: Child places the picture in the right group.

practical.title: Push or pull game
steps: Sort pictures into push and pull.
practical.safety: Keep fingers away from door hinges and drawers. Use only light doors and supervise closely.

differentiation.support: Do the action together and say the word.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find a push and a pull in the room.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Do we push or pull a swing?
Do we push or pull a wagon?

expectedOutcomes: Sorts actions into push and pull
Says push or pull with support
lessons.conclusion: Put away the cards and say "Push and pull."
lessons.homeConnection: Notice pushes and pulls at home, such as opening a door.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "decide if an action is a push or a pull" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Tug of war and trolley
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will use push and pull in a team game.
successCriteria: Pushes or pulls with a friend
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can explore materials, name animals and plants and care for living things.
lessons.starter: Say "Today we push and pull together. We are a team."
teacherActivities: Show how two children can push a trolley together.
Let pairs push the trolley to a cone.
Show how to pull a rope gently with a friend, with no tugging.
Talk about how it is easier together.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how two children can push a trolley together. Children: Children watch and say push.
Step 2. Teacher: Let pairs push the trolley to a cone. Children: Pair pushes the trolley together.
Step 3. Teacher: Show how to pull a rope gently with a friend, with no tugging. Children: Pair pulls the rope gently.
Step 4. Teacher: Talk about how it is easier together. Children: Child says easy or together.

practical.title: Team push and pull
steps: Set up a short path with cones.
Push a light trolley in pairs.
Pull a rope gently with a friend.
practical.safety: Never allow tugging or letting go suddenly. Use a soft rope and supervise every pair. Clear the floor.

differentiation.support: Work with the child and a friend and guide gently.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to count how many pushes it takes to reach the cone.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Is it easier alone or together?
What do we do with a trolley?

expectedOutcomes: Pushes and pulls with a friend
lessons.conclusion: Put the equipment away and say "We worked together."
lessons.homeConnection: Push and pull things together at home as a family.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "use push and pull in a team game" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 1 push and pull check
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child pushes and pulls and uses the words.
successCriteria: Pushes and pulls a toy on request
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can explore materials, name animals and plants and care for living things.
lessons.starter: Sing the push and pull song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: pushing, pulling and sorting.
At each station ask "Is it push or pull?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Child answers with a word or action.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: pushing, pulling and sorting. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "Is it push or pull?" Children: Child answers with a word or action.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Push and pull stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors clear. Use light objects only.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use one action.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to show a friend push and pull.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: pushes on request; pulls on request; says push or pull; sorts actions.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 1
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye with a push and a pull.
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about push and pull at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child pushes and pulls and uses the words" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
